entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Martial of Limoges, known as Marcial, Martialis, or Marcialis, was the first bishop of Limoges and the Apostle of the Gauls or Aquitaine. He played a crucial role in the early Christianization of Gaul. His significance lies in his leadership and influence on the development of Christianity in the region.


Martial was born unknown and died in 300 CE. His feast day is celebrated on June 30.


As the first bishop of Limoges, Martial established the city's first Christian church and promoted the spread of Christianity throughout the region. He also played a key role in the Roman Catholic Church's development and was considered a saint by the early Christian community.


Martial's legacy extends beyond his own time, as he contributed to the shaping of Christian doctrine and practice in Gaul. His influence can be seen in the development of the city of Limoges and the surrounding region, which became an important center of Christianity in the region.


The apostolic era of the Christian church in Gaul began with Martial, who brought Christianity to the pagan people of Aquitaine and established the church's first cathedral in Limoges. His feast day, June 30, has been celebrated as a day of martyrdom and devotion in the Christian calendar since the early centuries.
